metric_definitions.population: Every mean in this report is over POSITIVE queries only. Negative queries have no graded relevance, are scored 0 on all four metrics, and are reported separately in the negative-query block.
metric_definitions.precision_at_k: Fraction of the k returned rows that are labelled relevant.
metric_definitions.recall_at_k: Fraction of the query's labelled relevant documents that appear in the top k.
metric_definitions.mrr_at_k: Reciprocal rank of the FIRST relevant document within the top k, 0 when none is in the top k. The ranking is TRUNCATED to k before scoring, so MRR@1 is the hit-rate and MRR@5 is 0 for any query whose first relevant document ranks 6th or lower. MRR@10 over a 10-row corpus is the unbounded MRR.
metric_definitions.ndcg_at_k: Normalised discounted cumulative gain over the top k, with an ideal ranking of min(k, number of relevant documents).
metric_definitions.delta: Condition minus the same-corpus unprefixed baseline (condition A) at the same depth. No number here is comparable with the historical MRR 0.832, which was measured on a different corpus with a different harness.

reproduction.command: python3 -m bench prefix-experiment --output-dir /tmp/mpm-bench-issue23 --config bench/fixtures/nomic-embed-text.json --corpus-version v2 --conditions A,B,C,D
reproduction.note: The corpus version, the conditions and the config file are all recorded above; the same invocation reproduces this run.

scoring_parameters.note: Default HybridConfig at the v2 baseline. The retrieval_threshold of -3.0 is the log-space default; it is unreachable for 0-1 cosine similarity and the threshold check is therefore a no-op. The scoring uses the production ranker unchanged.

isolation.note: Every workspace is a disposable private temp dir with MPM_WORKSPACE and HOME pointed at it; the harness never falls back to the operator's installed binary or live DB.

limitations: The corpus is a 50-document / 60-query hand-authored synthetic set about MPM's own internals. Its scores are NOT comparable with the historical MRR 0.832, which was measured on a different (lost) corpus with a different (lost) harness.
The raw-cosine arm is not the MPM hybrid ranker. MPM blends FTS5 keyword scoring with the vector channel; the raw-cosine arm measures the vector channel alone.
The hybrid arm can only be measured in the unprefixed condition: MPM's recall path embeds the query verbatim, so a prefixed condition would require a production change.

In the document-prefixed conditions the corpus row's stored text carries the prefix (that is how the benchmark makes MPM's production embed path produce a prefixed vector). The stored text therefore also differs from production, which is why no hybrid measurement is taken in those workspaces.
Single model, single corpus, single run: no confidence intervals are computed. The per-query improved/regressed counts are the honest uncertainty signal.

The raw-cosine channel has no abstention path: a negative query always receives a full top-k. The irrelevant / no-answer behaviour is therefore measured on the MPM hybrid arm, and the raw-cosine error rate for negatives is reported as the top-1 similarity a negative query attracts.

A prefix change is a full re-embedding of the corpus in any future implementation. This experiment measures retrieval on a 50-document corpus; it does not measure the cost, the recall of already-stored vectors, or the behaviour of the live store, none of which are in scope for Phase A.
